reason: The story says the rough edge breaks the skin and a vessel, so the body needs to encounter it before the bleeding can be stopped.
expectation: The body will get a small cut that starts the bleeding response.

effect: The cut and narrowed vessel are now visible, so I can work on stopping the bleeding.
reaction: The vessel narrowing was a useful detail.
reason: The platelets are already at the cut, so they seem like the next pieces to use to stop the leak.
expectation: The platelets will gather at the damaged vessel and help plug it.

effect: The platelets formed a plug that slows the leak, but the bleeding goal is not yet complete.
reaction: It makes sense that the fragments gather at the break.
reason: The activated clotting factors and fibrinogen are both shown at the damaged vessel. I’m guessing they work together to strengthen the plug, though I don’t yet know how.
expectation: The clotting factors will change fibrinogen into material that helps strengthen the plug.

effect: The clotting factors changed fibrinogen into fibrin threads, which form a mesh among platelets.
reaction: The mesh makes the connection to strengthening the plug clearer.
reason: The fibrin threads are shown forming among platelets, so they should fit with the platelet plug at the cut.
expectation: The threads will reinforce the platelet plug and help stop the bleeding.

effect: The fibrin mesh reinforced the platelet plug and stopped the bleeding, but the skin remains open.
reaction: It was satisfying to see how the threads and platelets worked together, and the open skin leaves a clear next question.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding fibrin to the platelet plug was most worthwhile because it showed how the leak was sealed rather than just slowing down.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the cut was straightforward setup rather than an interesting choice, although it established the problem.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the vessel narrowed immediately after the cut, before the platelet plug formed.

arbitrary.text: Combining fibrinogen with activated clotting factors was initially a guess: their names suggested a connection, but I did not yet understand how they worked together.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the still-open skin heals after the bleeding stops.
